title: Prefill: KDA chain (core + conv + gated o_norm)
shape: DEP16 F16K (3 x 5,461 tok) at L78K, NVFP4 config (KDA in/o_proj MXFP8 -> o_norm writes the MXFP8 o_proj input), 96 KDA heads at TP1, FP32 state; per GPU per prefill forward, 69 KDA layers
basis: MEASURED microbench on 1 VR200 GPU at the deployed per-GPU shape, NVFP4 config (benchmarks/kimi_k3/bench_kda_prefill_chain.py, CUPTI kernel sums x 69): baseline 1118 us/layer, current 1054 us/layer (ab14); model nvfp4_modelopt|P3-16|prefill conv 55.1 + gate_beta_norm 18.4 + core_prefill 167.0 + o_norm 12.2 = 252.7 us/layer
gap_analysis: Per layer at F16K: recurrence K2 394 (stock FlashKDA mma.sync) + prepare K1 299 + Q|K|V conv 220 + o_norm/MXFP8 139 = 1054 us; model 253. The recurrence is a serial chain of 341 chunk steps per (seq, head) item and 288 items over 212 SMs, so its time is chunk-step LATENCY x 341, not throughput: model's 167 us core needs <= 0.49 us (1.1K clk) per step. Measured (in-kernel clock stamps): a tcgen05 chunk step costs MMA1 K=128 as dependent accumulating MMAs ~70 clk each, ~350 clk per tensor-core hand-off, plus single-warp-per-SMSP SIMT; stock mma.sync K2 = 1.16 us/step (HMMA rate is 1/4 of tcgen05, measured). Remaining after K2: K1 299 (latency-bound single-shot CTAs), conv 220 (at HBM rate), o_norm 139 (at ~7 TB/s); these are throughput work that must run concurrently with the latency-bound recurrence (same kernel / co-resident) to approach the model.
inefficiencies: MEASURED: K2 recurrence 394 us/layer: legacy mma.sync + per-chunk FP32->BF16 state fragment conversions/transposes, 1.36 items per SM (no ncu in the image to split latency vs pipe)
MEASURED: K1 prepare 299 us/layer: latency-bound single-shot CTAs; writes ~1.2 GB workspace that K2 re-reads
MEASURED: conv pass 220 us/layer (2.4 GB at HBM rate); fusion into today's K1 is slower (728 vs 518 us)
MEASURED: o_norm/MXFP8 139 us (fixed from 203; floor ~85 us)
rubin_features: bulk tensor copies (TMA) for the FusedConv raw Q|K|V boxes (exp branch)
packed FP32 FMA/mul/add (fma.rn.f32x2) in the conv + SiLU (IEEE per lane)

planned: tcgen05 MMA with the FP32 state as a TMEM accumulator (kind::f16 BF16 operands, stock FlashKDA chunk-16 math) for the 96-head recurrence; persistent TMA-ring K1; larger per-SM shared memory for multi-tile K1 rings
plan: DONE (landed-ready 47bc2f317f): HBM-rate gated o_norm + MXFP8 kernel: -59 us/layer F16K

SOL design (one persistent kernel per layer): per SM 1-2 (seq, head) items; loader warps TMA the raw q|k|v|g|beta rows (conv halo from the previous chunk), conv + gate cumsum + L2 norm + kd/qd/kr + INV/Mqk prep warps fill an smem ring (K1 work, no workspace in HBM), recurrence warps run the chunk chain on tcgen05 with the fp32 state row-per-thread in registers and bf16 S^T as the tensor-memory A operand, epilogue warps do gated o_norm + MXFP8. HBM traffic = raw activations in + MXFP8 out (~2.0 GB, ~160 us); recurrence = 341 serial chunk steps per item, must be <= ~0.45 us/step to hide under the bytes
Step 1 (in progress): tcgen05 recurrence (k2_tc.cuh, mode bit 5) on the unchanged K1 workspace; target K2 394 -> <= ~170 us
Step 2: cut the chunk-step latency (fine-grained K-slice pipelining of the state update into MMA1, MMA issue overlap) using in-kernel clock stamps
Step 3: move K1 prep (+ FusedConv from wzhao/k31ws-p-kda-fusedconv-exp) into producer warps of the recurrence kernel (removes K1 299 + conv 220 us and the workspace round trip)
Step 4: o_norm + MXFP8 epilogue inside the recurrence kernel (removes the 139 us pass)
